claim_text: Püskürtme betonun tünel desteğindeki başlıca işlevleri şunlardır:

* **Yüzey Koruma ve Stabilizasyon:** Kazının hemen ardından uygulanarak, kaya ortamında oluşabilecek sökülme ve gevşemeleri engeller; kazılan yüzeylerin hava ve su ile temasını keserek yüzey bozunmasını önler [E001][E004].

* **Kemerleşme ve Yük Taşıma:** Uzun vadede, ilave püskürtme beton tabakaları ve kaya bulonları ile birlikte çevredeki kaya ortamını yük taşıyabilir bir kemer haline dönüştürerek uzun dönem duraylılığını güvence altına alır [E001]. Kırık ve çatlaklar arasına girerek kayacın yerindeki kayma dayanımını artırır ve zayıf bağlantılı kaya elemanları arasında statik bir kabuk gibi çalışarak taşıyıcılık sağlar [E001][E004].

* **Deformasyon Kontrolü:** Çöken veya gevşeyen tabakalara karşı erken direnç göstererek iyi bir kemerleşme sağlar; dayanımın zamanla artmasıyla gevşemeleri önler ve deformasyonları en aza indirir [E001][E004].

* **Rijitlik ve Dayanım Artırma:** Kaya kütlelerinin boşluklarını (çatlak, eklem vb.) doldurarak rijitliklerini ve dayanımlarını artırır; kaya kütlelerinin yüklerini bitişik stabil kayalara aktarır [E005].
* **Erken Destek:** Özellikle zayıf kaya ve zemin koşullarında, sökülmelere ve hızlı deformasyonlara izin vermeden kazı takibinde hızlı bir biçimde uygulanarak stabilizasyon sağlar [E001].
Kaya bulonu, tünel tahkimatında ana destek elemanlarından biri olarak aşağıdaki görevleri üstlenir:

* **Taşıyıcı Halka Oluşturma ve Makaslama Dayanımını Artırma:** Kaya bulonları, tünel kazı yüzeyine sistematik olarak ışınsal olarak uygulanarak, kazı çevresinde taşıyıcı halka olarak tarif edilen bölgede kaya ortamının makaslama dayanımını arttırmaktadır [E002].
* **Deplasman Önleme ve Ufalanmayı Engelleme:** Oluşması muhtemel aşırı deplasmanları önlemekte, ufalanma ve dağılmaları engelleyerek etkin ve taşıyıcı bir yapı oluşturmaktadır [E002].

* **Püskürtme Beton ile Etkileşim:** Taşıyıcı plakaları püskürtme beton yüzeyine basarak, püskürtme betonun oluşturduğu kabuğun altındaki katmanlara oturmasını ve kaya kemeri ile birlikte çalışmasını sağlar [E002].

* **Gerilme Durumu ve Sürtünme Direnci:** Kayada üç eksenli gerilme halini meydana getirmek, çekme gerilmelerini ana kayaya aktarmak ve süreksizlik oluşan bölgelerde sürtünme direncini yükseltmek amacıyla kullanılır [E004][E010].

* **Kaya Bloklarının Sabitlenmesi:** Tünel kazısı esnasında tavanda veya duvarda kopmak üzere olan, ayrışmış kayaların konumlarını korumalarına yardımcı olarak güvenliği arttıran destek elemanıdır [E004][E010].
* **Enjeksiyon ile Destek:** Zeminin içindeki ana kemerleşmeyi enjeksiyonla birlikte sağlayarak, kayanın kayma dayanımını arttırır [E002].
Tünellerde çelik iksa (çelik bağ), aşağıdaki amaçlarla kullanılır:

* **Geçici Destek ve Güvenlik:** Püskürtme betonun dayanımını kazanıncaya kadar geçen sürede yapım güvenliğini sağlamak ve çalışma emniyetini kontrol etmek amacıyla uygulanır [E001][E005][E012][E017][E018].

* **Yük Dağılımı ve Donatı:** Püskürtme betonda yük dağılımına yardımcı olmak, taze püskürtme beton yük taşımaya başlamadan önce destek sağlamak ve betonun mukavemetini kazandıktan sonra çelik hasırla birlikte kalıcı donatı teşkil etmek amacıyla kullanılır [E001][E005][E009][E012][E017][E018][E020].
* **Deformasyon Kontrolü:** Tünel cidarının aşırı deformasyonunu önlemek, kayanın gevşemesine engel olmak ve küçük kaya düşmelerini engellemek amacıyla uygulanır [E012][E018].
* **Diğer Elemanlara Mesnet:** Sürgü çubuğuna (süren) destek vermek, kaya bulonlarının ön gerilme kuvvetlerini dağıtmak ve süren kazıklara destek teşkil etmek amacıyla kullanılır [E012][E020].

* **Yapısal Koruma:** Tünel kesitini düşey ve yanal basınçlara karşı korumak, örselenmiş veya hareket halindeki zemin/kaya ağırlığını taşımak ve kısmi bir dengeleme basıncı gerçekleştirerek kırılma ile genleşme tehlikesini önlemek amacıyla uygulanır [E012].
* **Uygunluk:** Çok zayıf zeminlerde profil çelik iksalar veya yüksek deformasyonların olduğu durumlarda U profiller tercih edilebilmektedir [E012][E017][E018].
Yeni Avusturya Tünel Açma Yöntemi (NATM) temel prensipleri şunlardır:

* Tünelin su geçirimsizliğinin sağlanması ve sızıntı olması durumunda onarımlar için önlemlerin alınması [E002].

* **İç Yüzeyi Düzenlemek:** Tünel içinde üniform (düzgün) bir iç yüzey sağlar [E001][E003]. Bu düzgün yüzey; hava akışı, estetik aydınlatma ve bakım gereklilikleri için önemlidir [E001][E003].
* **Su Geçirimsizliği:** Tünel kaplamasının su geçirimsizliğini artırır [E001][E003].
* **Yapısal Destek ve Uzun Ömür:** Tünelin tasarım ömrü boyunca çalışmasını sağlar ve duraylılığı uzun süre sağlayacak şekilde projelendirilen destek sistemidir [E002][E003].
* **Deformasyonu Azaltmak:** Dış kaplama sırasında oluşan deformasyonları iç kaplama ile en aza indirger [E003].

* **Yüzey Hazırlığı ve Koruma:** Tünelin son kullanım amacına (estetik, akış karakteristiği vb.) hazırlamak için düzgün ve dayanıklı bir zemin oluşturur; aynı zamanda yeraltı sularının sızmasını önler ve nihai betonu zararlı kimyasal maddelere karşı korur [E003][E007].
Tünel portalı, tünelin giriş ve çıkış ağızlarında inşa edilen ve zeminin topografik ile jeolojik özelliklerine uygun projelendirilmesi gereken bir sanat yapısıdır [E002].
Portalde meydana gelebilecek olumsuzluklar, tünel içi çalışmaları durdurabileceği gibi iş ve işçi güvenliğini de tehdit edebilir [E002].

Jeoteknik etüt çalışmalarında yapılan araştırmalar, proje aşamasına (ön etüt, ön proje, kesin proje) ve uygulama evresine göre değişmekle birlikte, sağlanan kanıtlara göre aşağıdaki başlıklar altında toplanabilir:
**1. Arazi ve Haritalama Çalışmaları:**
* Jeolojik haritalama (mühendislik jeolojisi) yapılır; birimler tanımlanır, ayrışma, bozulma, dayanım ve süreksizlikler belirlenir [E008].
* Arazi çalışmaları kapsamında jeolojik haritalama, birim tanımlamaları ve süreksizlik tabloları hazırlanır [E005].
* Yüzey jeolojisi incelemeleri, hava fotoğrafı çalışmaları ve mevcut verilerin derlenmesi/planlanması yapılır [E017].
**2. Sondaj ve Yerinde Deneyler:**
* Temel araştırma sondajları yapılır; yerinde deneyler uygulanır, yeraltı suyu seviyesi takip edilir ve örnekler düzenlenir [E010].
* Sondaj programı yapılır ve sondaj logları elde edilir [E005].
* Yerinde deneyler ile kaya mukavemeti ve diğer parametreler belirlenmeye çalışılır [E015].
**3. Jeofizik Araştırmalar:**

* Tünel jeolojik-jeoteknik etütleri kapsamında jeofizik çalışmaları yürütülür. Bu çalışmaların amacı; jeolojik birimlerin altere kesimleri/fay zonları, karstik boşluklar ve yeraltı suyu seviyesinin belirlenmesidir [E001].
* Jeofizik araştırmalar genellikle Sismik Kırılma ve Elektrik Özdirenç yöntemleriyle yapılır; gerektiğinde Jeoradar yöntemi de kullanılır [E011].
* Jeofizik çalışmaların hazırlık aşamasında doğru ekipman temini, amaca uygun yöntem ve açılımların sağlanması ve veri elde edilmesi hedeflenir [E010].
**4. Laboratuvar Çalışmaları:**
* Laboratuvar deney programı hazırlanır ve uygulanır; standartlara uygun veri sağlanır [E010].
* Jeolojik birimlerin jeoteknik özellikleri (RMR, Q ve GSI sınıflandırmaları, tek eksenli basma dayanımı, elastisite modülü, Poisson oranı vb.) laboratuvar deneyleri ile belirlenir [E005].
**5. Jeolojik ve Jeoteknik Modelleme ile Raporlama:**
* Elde edilen veriler (arazi, sondaj, laboratuvar) kullanılarak jeolojik model oluşturulur ve tünel jeolojik-jeoteknik raporu hazırlanır [E010].
* Rapor; genel jeoloji, mühendislik jeolojisi, hidrojeoloji, kaya sınıflandırmaları (RMR, Q, GSI), jeomekanik değerlendirmeler ve kritik kesitlerin belirlenmesini içerir [E008].
* Jeoteknik model kurulur; kritik enkesitler belirlenir ve bu kesimlerdeki jeoteknik birim özellikleri çıkarılır [E005].
**6. İnşaat Sırası Ek Çalışmalar (Yansıtma ve İzleme):**
* Tünel açılımı sırasında tünel kazı aynasından elde edilen jeolojik veriler (jeolojik birimler, süreksizlikler, su durumu, kaya kalitesi vb.) izlenir [E015].
* Jeoteknik değerlendirme yapılır; Kaya Kütle Değeri (RMR) hesaplanır ve kazı destek sınıfı belirlenir [E015].
* Deformasyon ölçümleri (yerinde arazi ölçümleri) yapılır [E017].
* Karşılaşılan problemler raporlanır ve jeolojik dokümantasyon (1:100 ölçekli haritalama) gerçekleştirilir [E012].

claim_text: The primary function of the shield in a Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) is to protect the machine and provide immediate support to the excavated face, thereby controlling ground loss and settlement.
Specific functions include:

* **Face Stability:** In soft ground applications, the shield (particularly closed-face machines) prevents groundwater and unconsolidated ground from entering the tunnel at the excavated face [E001][E002]. It helps balance ground and groundwater pressures to minimize settlement [E001].
* **Protection:** The shield protects the internal components of the TBM and workers from the surrounding ground, especially in unstable or squeezing rock conditions [E004][E009].

* **Support for Lining:** The shield provides a protected space within which precast concrete segments can be erected to form the tunnel lining [E001][E002]. The machine advances by thrusting hydraulic jacks against these assembled segment rings within the tail shield [E001].

* **Annulus Management:** The shield's diameter is slightly larger than the assembled ring, creating an annulus that must be filled with grout to minimize potential for settlement as the machine advances [E001].

* **Reaction Force:** In some configurations, such as single shield TBMs, the shield allows thrust cylinders to extend and drive the machine forward by pushing against the last completed segment ring [E009].

The primary purpose of a tunnel drainage system is to remove water from the roadway and prevent it from coming into contact with the completed tunnel lining, which can cause safety problems and increased maintenance costs [E002][E010].

Specifically, the system collects and disposes of water that enters the tunnel through groundwater infiltration via cracks in the lining, surface waters entering through portals or vent shafts (including flooding), and water used for periodic preventative washing of the roadway [E008].
Additionally, the drainage system serves to:
* Remove water from the roadway to mitigate hazards such as hydroplaning, engine stalling, and reduced visibility [E008].
* Collect spilled fuel and oil to prevent risks of fire or explosion, requiring the use of noncombustible pipes during emergencies [E008].
* Capture mountain water and channel it within the tunnel cross-section to maintain operation and keep operating costs low [E010].
The main components of a road tunnel ventilation system include:
* **Fans:** The primary component, which can be axial (tube or vane) for longitudinal systems or centrifugal for transverse and semi-transverse systems [E003].
* **Motors:** Electric motors (constant or variable speed) that drive the fans [E003][E008].
* **Ductwork and Airways:** Supply and exhaust ducts (in transverse systems) or the tunnel bore itself acting as ductwork (in longitudinal systems), including plenums and flues [E001][E003].
* **Dampers:** Devices to control airflow, which can be motor-operated (MOD) and may be fully open, closed, or intermediate [E003][E005].
* **Louvers:** Used at air intake structures and exhaust points to control airflow entry/exit [E003][E016].
* **Sound Attenuators:** Installed to mitigate noise, either mounted directly to fans or within ductwork [E003][E005].
* **Control Panels and Conduit:** For system operation and monitoring [E005].
* **Air Quality Monitoring Equipment:** Such as carbon monoxide (CO) sensors to adjust ventilation based on traffic and air quality [E002][E005].
* **Power Source:** Electrical supply for fans, motors, and controls [E004].
* **Drive Trains:** Direct or indirect (belts, chains, gears) connections between motors and fans [E008].
Rock mass classification systems are primarily used to assess ground behavior and define the support required to stabilize a tunnel opening [E001].
Specifically, they serve several functions in tunnel design:
* **Support Design:** They provide a basis for estimating deformation and strength properties, supplying quantitative data for support estimation, and determining tunnel supports [E003][E004].
* **Communication Platform:** They present a platform for communication between exploration, design, and construction groups [E004].
* **Method Selection:** They help in the preliminary evaluation of the most appropriate tunnelling method (Conventional vs. Mechanized) by considering geological setting and rock mass quality [E002].
* **Performance Prediction:** They are used in empirical models to predict Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) performance, including penetration rate and advance rate [E004][E014].
* **Parameter Estimation:** They are used to estimate the in situ deformation modulus of a rock mass, which is essential for design and analysis [E020].

* **Process-Oriented Design:** In methods like SEM (NATM), they assist in deriving Ground Response Classes (GRC) and Excavation and Support Classes (ESC) to define excavation sequences and support measures [E001].

However, it is noted that these systems were originally developed for rock mass characterization and support design in classical tunneling, not specifically to describe rock mass boreability for TBM performance, which can lead to limited accuracy in such predictions [E005][E014].
Additionally, they cannot replace thorough design by experienced engineers and must be based on thorough ground investigation [E001].
The primary purpose of geotechnical and structural instrumentation in tunnelling is to monitor the performance of the underground construction process to avoid or mitigate problems [E001].
Specifically, instrumentation serves several key roles:

* **Safety and Stability Assessment:** It tracks movements and stresses to determine if support or construction processes need modification, ensuring short-term safety and long-term stability of the completed tunnel [E006]. It assesses system stability and the impact on the environment, validating the appropriateness of excavation and support measures [E007].

* **Verification of Design:** In methods like the Sequential Excavation Method (SEM), monitoring is integral for verifying design assumptions regarding ground-support interaction and optimizing the support concept to reduce costs and risks [E003][E007].

* **Damage Prevention:** It provides data to determine the source and magnitude of ground movements, helping to prevent or minimize damage to existing structures and the structure under construction [E002].

* **Risk Management:** A good monitoring program supports risk analysis and management, potentially paying for itself by preventing major incidents [E002]. It helps identify if observed system behavior lies within expected limits and allows for the prediction of system behavior and updating of geological models [E007].

* **Decision Support:** Monitoring data assists in selecting appropriate remedial measures, evaluating critical design assumptions, assessing contractor performance, and providing documentation for potential disputes or damages [E002].
In summary, instrumentation transforms raw readings into usable data to inform decisions on whether mitigative actions are required when movements or stresses reach pre-set trigger levels [E001].

Cut-and-cover tunnel construction is a method used for shallow-depth tunnels where a trench is excavated from the surface, the tunnel structure is built within that excavation, and the site is subsequently covered with backfill material [E001][E003].
The process typically involves braced, trench-type excavation ("cut") followed by the placement of fill materials over the finished structure ("cover") [E001][E014].
Key characteristics and procedures include:

* **Depth and Application:** It is generally used for relatively shallow tunnels, typically with less than 45 to 60 feet (14 to 18 meters) of overburden, though depths up to 100 feet (30 m) are sometimes encountered [E001][E003]. It is commonly used for subway lines, stations, subsurface highways, underpasses, and approaches to mined or subaqueous tunnels [E001][E003].
* **Construction Sequences:** There are two primary methods:

* **Bottom-Up:** A trench is excavated using temporary support walls (such as soldier piles, sheet piling, or slurry walls), the tunnel structure (floor, walls, and roof) is constructed inside, waterproofing is applied to the exterior, and the trench is backfilled [E003][E008]. This method allows for easier access and external waterproofing but requires a larger footprint and delays surface restoration [E003][E008].

* **Top-Down:** Permanent or temporary support walls (slurry or secant piles) are constructed first, followed by the tunnel roof slab. The surface is then restored while excavation continues beneath the roof to construct the floor and interior [E013][E016]. This method allows for early surface restoration and reduced construction width but complicates external waterproofing and slab connections [E013][E016].

* **Structure:** Cut-and-cover tunnels are typically designed as rigid frame box structures, often made of cast-in-place reinforced concrete, though precast concrete and structural steel are also used [E003][E006]. They may be rectangular in cross-section, with subway stations often being two- or three-story structures [E001][E006].

* **Disadvantages:** A major disadvantage is the widespread disruption to surface traffic and urban activities during construction, as the ground cannot be fully restored until the structure is complete (in bottom-up methods) or significant surface work is required [E002][E003].
An immersed tube tunnel is a construction method employed to traverse a body of water, such as a canal, channel, bay, or river [E001][E002].
The construction process involves fabricating large pre-cast concrete or concrete-filled steel tunnel sections off-site in dry docks, shipyards, or floodable basins [E004][E010].
These sections are sealed with bulkheads at each end to make them watertight and are then floated out [E004][E010].
The sections are towed to the tunnel site, placed into a pre-excavated trench, jointed together, and ballasted or anchored [E001][E004].
Finally, the trench is backfilled with soil or engineered fill to protect the tunnel and resist buoyancy [E001][E002].

* **Installation:** Segments are erected inside the tail shield of a TBM. The TBM thrust rams act on prepared sections of the ring to advance the excavation [E001][E002].
* **Types:**

* **Initial Lining (Two-Pass):** Often lightly reinforced, rough cast, and erected without bolting or waterproofing. The ring is jacked apart to fill the annular space, followed by contact grouting and a cast-in-place final lining [E002][E008].

* **Final Lining (One-Pass):** Built to high tolerances, heavily reinforced, and fitted with gaskets for waterproofing. Segments are bolted together to compress the gaskets, and contact grouting is performed as the ring leaves the TBM shield [E002][E008].

* **Design Considerations:** The primary load is axial force from ground and hydrostatic pressures. Design must account for significant construction loads, including TBM jacking forces, lifting/erecting loads (dead weight with a dynamic factor of 2.0), and grouting pressure (recommended max 10 psi) [E005][E008].

* **Advantages:** They provide immediate, stable ground support; materials are easy to transport and handle inside the tunnel; no formwork or curing is required prior to use; and they provide a durable, low-maintenance structure [E002].

* **Disadvantages:** Segments must be fabricated to very tight tolerances; they require storage space at the job site; and they can be damaged (spalling, cracking) if mishandled or over-jacked [E002].

The excavation and support sequence in the Sequential Excavation Method (SEM), also known as the New Austrian Tunneling Method (NATM), is organized through a flexible, observational process that integrates ground behavior with support installation.
The sequence is defined by the following key elements:

**1. Classification and Planning** The process begins with a thorough ground investigation to classify the ground and define excavation and support classes based on rock mass conditions [E001][E002]. This classification determines the specific parameters for each round of excavation [E001][E002].
**2. Excavation Strategy**
* **Subdivision:** The tunnel cross-section is subdivided into multiple drifts or headings as needed, such as a top heading, bench, and invert (or side wall drifts) [E001][E002].
* **Round Length:** The maximum unsupported excavation length (round length) is defined based on ground stability and stand-up time [E001][E002].
* **Sequencing:** In weak ground or large sections, excavation often proceeds in stages (e.g., top heading followed by bench and invert) to maintain stability [E009][E012].

claim_text: The primary techniques include:
**1. Dewatering and Drainage**
* **Face Dewatering:** The most common method for rock tunnels involves allowing water to drain into the tunnel through the face, collecting it, and pumping it out via channels or sumps [E012].
* **Probe Holes:** Drill holes ahead of the tunnel face can pre-drain rock, provide warning of gas or contaminants, and reduce water inflow [E012][E011].
* **Pilot Tunnels:** Smaller exploratory tunnels can be used to drain groundwater and assess water volumes before main excavation [E011].

* **Construction Dewatering:** For cut-and-cover or open excavations, water tables are lowered using well-points, deep wells, or sump pumps. Impervious retaining walls (e.g., slurry walls) may be used to cut off water flow [E003].
* **Recharge Wells:** To mitigate settlement from external dewatering, pumped water can be reinjected into bearing strata via injection wells [E003].
**2. Groundwater Cut-off and Sealing**

* **Grouting:** This is the most common method for controlling inflow in rock tunnels, particularly at joints and fractures. It involves injecting cement, chemical, or micro-fine grouts to seal water pathways [E011][E018].
* **Impervious Walls:** Steel sheeting, concrete slurry walls, or tangent piles can be installed to reduce groundwater inflow and limit draw-down during construction [E003].

* **Ground Freezing:** Used as a "last resource" or for specific localized issues (e.g., TBM launch chambers), freezing creates a groundwater cut-off and stabilizes soil. It is generally uneconomical for long rock tunnels due to high flow velocities exceeding freezing feasibility, but effective in complex urban soft ground [E011][E018].
**3. Tunneling Machine and Face Pressure Control**

* **Pressurized Face TBMs:** Closed face machines (Earth Pressure Balance or Slurry Face Machines) maintain pressure at the tunnel face equal to or greater than groundwater head, preventing drawdown and inflow [E013][E007].
* **Compressed Air:** Historically used to stabilize faces and control water, it is now rare due to complexity but may still be used for low-pressure stabilization [E006].
**4. Waterproofing Systems (Permanent)**

* **Open/Drained Systems:** Used in rock tunnels with low infiltration. An umbrella-like waterproofing drains water seeping into the tunnel to a drainage system at the invert, reducing hydrostatic load on the lining [E002].

* **Closed/Tanked Systems:** Used in permeable soils to completely exclude groundwater. These systems encapsulate the tunnel perimeter, requiring secondary linings designed for full hydrostatic pressure [E002].
* **Segmental Linings:** Precast segments often use gaskets to seal joints and provide watertightness [E002].
**5. Other Measures**
* **Panning:** Placing pans over specific leaks or seams and channeling water to the invert drainage system [E006].
* **Drainage Fabric:** Geotechnical fabrics placed over rock surfaces to provide drainage pathways into collection systems at the invert, sandwiched between rock and concrete lining [E006].

Tunnel lining design and construction involve selecting materials and methods based on ground conditions, excavation techniques, and functional requirements to provide structural support, limit water inflow, and ensure long-term durability.
**Design Considerations**

* **Interaction with Ground:** Tunnel linings are structural systems that interact with surrounding ground. Their stability depends on this interaction; flexibility and ductility allow the lining to deform as the ground deforms, mobilizing ground strength and redistributing loads into axial thrust rather than bending moments [E002].

* **Design Philosophy:** Design typically utilizes Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD) specifications, such as those from the AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, to account for variability in loads and structural behavior [E001].

* **Durability and Safety:** Linings must withstand long-term exposure, including extreme events like fires. Protection is achieved through concrete cover, finishes, and the inclusion of plastic fibers in mixes to prevent spalling [E002].

* **Waterproofing:** Systems are designed to control groundwater inflow, using either drained (open) systems that allow localized seepage into drainage channels or undrained (closed/tanked) systems that exclude water entirely, requiring the lining to resist full hydrostatic pressure [E017].
**Lining Types and Selection** The choice of lining system depends on ground conditions, tunneling method, and geometry [E003]. Common types include:

* **Cast-in-Place Concrete:** Used in hard and soft ground, often as a final lining after initial support. It can be formed into any shape (circular, rectangular, horseshoe) and is frequently used in two-pass systems with TBMs or drill-and-blast methods [E001][E003].

* **Precast Segmental Lining:** Used exclusively with Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs) in a single-pass system. Segments are circular arcs assembled inside the TBM shield, featuring gaskets for watertightness and tight manufacturing tolerances [E001][E003].

* **Steel Plate Lining:** A segmental system where steel plates form rings, often used in soft ground TBMs. It provides immediate support but is susceptible to corrosion and fire damage, often requiring a protective concrete layer [E001][E009].

* **Shotcrete:** Pneumatically applied concrete used as initial support or, with advanced technology, as a permanent final lining (e.g., in Sequential Excavation Method/SEM tunnels). It can be reinforced with steel fibers, plastic fibers, or lattice girders [E001][E012].
**Construction Methods**
* **Initial Support:** Often provided by shotcrete, rock bolts, steel ribs, or lagging to stabilize the heading immediately after excavation [E005].
* **Final Lining Installation:**
* *Cast-in-Place:* Forms are installed against a waterproofing membrane, reinforced steel is placed, and concrete is poured. Curing occurs before form removal [E003].
* *Precast Segments:* Segments are erected inside the TBM tail shield to form rings. Joints are bolted and gasketed [E001][E008].
* *Steel Plates:* Curved steel elements are assembled and bolted together inside the TBM, with gaskets compressed to seal joints [E009].
* *Shotcrete Final Lining:* Applied in layers against a waterproofing membrane, often used for complex geometries or short tunnels where formwork is uneconomical [E019].

* **Dual Lining (SEM):** Involves an initial shotcrete layer and a final cast-in-place or shotcrete layer, with a waterproofing membrane sandwiched between them. The geometry is curvilinear to activate the self-supporting arch in the ground [E012].

**Constructability Factors** Design must facilitate construction within limited space, ensuring materials are small enough to handle and negotiate tunnel geometry. Construction procedures must account for moist or wet conditions and ensure that the tunnel length remains available for operations as much as possible [E002].
Soft ground tunneling employs several construction methods, selected based on geological conditions, depth, and project requirements:

* **Shield Tunneling:** This includes various types of shields such as blind shields, open face hang-dug shields, semi-mechanized shields, fully mechanized shields, slurry face machines (SFM), and earth pressure balance (EPB) machines. Modern pressurized-face closed shield TBMs, specifically EPB and SFM types, are predominantly used for large diameter soft ground tunneling [E003].

* **Sequential Excavation Method (SEM) / New Austrian Tunneling Method (NATM):** Soft ground tunnels can be excavated sequentially by small drifts and openings following SEM principles. This method is viable for short tunnels, large openings (such as stations), unusual shapes, complex structures like intersections, and enlargements [E001][E006].

* **Cut-and-Cover:** This method is adopted for shallow tunnels where safe excavation from the surface is possible without collapsing walls and when it is economical. It involves excavating a trench, constructing the structure (in-situ or precast), and backfilling. It is commonly used for underpasses, approach sections of other tunnels, and in flat terrain or shallow depth [E002][E008].

* **Immersed Tunnels:** These consist of large pre-cast concrete or concrete-filled steel elements fabricated on land, floated to the site, installed in a prepared trench under water, and backfilled. They are used for road or rail connections crossing water bodies [E001][E008].

* **Jacked Box Tunnels:** Prefabricated box structures are jacked horizontally through the soil against a thrust wall, often using bentonite slurry to reduce surface friction. This method is used in soft ground for short lengths, particularly beneath runways or railroad embankments where surface disturbance must be minimized [E001][E008].
Tunnel inspection and maintenance are organized through distinct but integrated organizational structures, personnel roles, and procedural frameworks as detailed in the evidence.

**Organizational Structure for Inspection** The National Tunnel Inspection Standards (NTIS) require State, Federal Land, and Tribal governments to establish a dedicated tunnel inspection organization [E015]. This organization is led by a Program Manager, who must be a registered professional engineer or have at least 10 years of experience and is nationally certified [E003][E014]. The Program Manager develops written procedures, schedules inspections, and ensures NTIS compliance [E014]. Field operations are supervised by Team Leaders, who coordinate inspections and report to the Program Manager [E003][E014]. Inspection teams may also include Discipline Specialists, Inspectors, and Specialty Contractors for complex systems [E014]. Crucially, the operating and maintenance personnel of the tunnel facility are not used for inspection purposes to ensure independent assessment [E014].

**Organizational Structure for Maintenance and Operations** Tunnel owners or authorities must establish an organizational structure for technical maintenance, fire/rescue procedures, and traffic operation [E009]. This operational organization is responsible for updating procedures to handle acute problems (accidents, technical failures), routine service and maintenance, and planning for major repairs [E009]. Staffing varies based on facility size, location, and traffic levels, often requiring 24-hour coverage with three shifts for full operation [E013]. Key roles include:
* **Tunnel Manager:** Manages the facility, budgets, contracts, and personnel [E001].
* **Facility Engineer:** Leads technical programs, maintenance programs, and capital improvements [E001].
* **Tunnel Supervisor:** Manages day-to-day operations, generates work assignments, schedules repairs, and responds to incidents [E001].
* **Tunnel Operators:** Monitor traffic, congestion, and functional systems (ventilation, lighting, CCTV) [E001][E018].
* **Specialists:** Mechanical, electrical, and electronics specialists perform routine maintenance on specific systems [E018].
* **Safety/Security Officers:** Coordinate emergency response, conduct drills, and manage security protocols [E018].
**Inspection Procedures and Types** Inspections are categorized into specific types with defined purposes and intervals [E007][E019]:
* **Initial Inspection:** Establishes baseline conditions for new tunnels (prior to opening) or existing tunnels (within 24 months of NTIS effective date) [E019].
* **Routine Inspection:** Comprehensive observations and measurements performed every 24 months (extendable to 48 months with justification) to monitor condition changes [E007][E019].
* **Damage Inspection:** Performed after events like impacts, fires, or floods; the tunnel remains closed until this inspection is complete [E019].
* **In-Depth and Special Inspections:** In-depth inspections are scheduled by the program manager for complex systems; special inspections monitor critical safety defects [E007].
Daily or frequent checks by inspection teams verify that facilities (lighting, fans) are functioning, the tunnel is clean, and there are no cracks, leaks, or deformations [E002].
**Maintenance Activities and Strategies** Maintenance is organized into Preventive, Corrective (On-Demand), and Rehabilitation activities [E006][E008]:

* **Preventive Maintenance:** Aimed at preventing failure, this includes cyclical (pre-determined intervals), conditional (based on wear indicators), and predictive (data-driven) methods [E006][E008]. Good practice suggests 70-80% of maintenance should be preventive [E006].
* **Corrective/On-Demand Maintenance:** Addresses difficult-to-predict occurrences like vehicle impacts or sudden equipment malfunctions [E006].
* **Rehabilitation:** Large-scale repairs for systems near the end of their useful life, such as overhauling ventilation or upgrading fire suppression [E006].
Routine maintenance tasks include cleaning (tunnel washing, debris removal), crack sealing, joint repair, and servicing equipment like jet fans, lighting, and drainage systems [E002][E004][E006].
Maintenance planning considers life-cycle costs, with technical equipment often having a 10-20 year service life compared to the structure's 100+ years [E008].

claim_text: Based on the provided evidence, the following ventilation strategies are used for smoke control in road tunnels:

**1. Longitudinal Ventilation** Longitudinal ventilation systems move air in the same direction as traffic flow. This strategy is commonly used to control smoke during emergencies by maintaining specific air velocities to prevent backlayering and keep smoke stratified [E001]. Key configurations include:

* **Jet Fan Systems:** High-velocity axial fans are mounted at the ceiling to induce longitudinal airflow. This method was approved by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) in 1995 based on the Memorial Tunnel Fire Ventilation Test Program [E002][E003].
* **Central Fan Systems (Saccardo Nozzles):** These systems use high-velocity nozzles to inject air into the tunnel [E003].
**2. Transverse Ventilation** Transverse systems use separate ducts for supply and exhaust air, isolating the traffic tube from the ventilation airflow. Strategies include:

* **Full Transverse:** Features both supply and exhaust air ducts located above, below, or to the side of the traffic tube. Fresh air is injected at regular intervals, and contaminants are removed via exhaust ducts [E003].

* **Semi-Transverse:** Uses either a supply duct or an exhaust duct, with the tunnel bore acting as the intake or exhaust for the other. The traffic opening takes over some of the duties of a supply duct [E003].

**3. Natural Ventilation** Natural ventilation relies on meteorological conditions (elevation/temperature differences between portals and prevailing winds) and the piston effect from traffic to move air. While simple, many naturally ventilated tunnels install axial fans specifically for fire and smoke emergencies to enhance control [E017].

**4. Single-Point Extraction** This strategy is used in conjunction with semi- or full-transverse systems to increase airflow during a fire. It involves remotely controlled louvers that increase the opening size of exhaust flues to manage smoke more effectively during emergencies [E017].
**Operational Strategies for Smoke Control**

* **Preventing Backlayering:** Ventilation strategies are selected based on tunnel type, system capacity, and traffic levels to optimize smoke management. The primary goal is to prevent backlayering (smoke moving against the ventilation flow) and maintain smoke stratification as long as possible to aid self-rescue [E001].
* **Automatic Incident Detection (AID):** The use of AID systems is strongly recommended to reduce detection and intervention delays, thereby facilitating self-rescue by road users [E004][E007].

* **Emergency Exit Utilization:** In tunnels without longitudinal ventilation, the presence of emergency exits is critical for safety. Strategies include enforcing the use of these exits through facilities and signage to ensure self-rescue [E004][E007].

claim_text: Based on the provided evidence, these factors include:
**1. Geological and Geotechnical Conditions**

* **Ground Type:** The nature of the material (rock, soft ground, mixed face) is a primary determinant. Rock tunnels may use drill-and-blast or Tunnel Boring Machines (TBM), while soft ground often requires shielded machines, Earth Pressure Balance Machines (EPBMs), or Slurry Face Machines (SFM) [E001][E004].
* **Rock Mass Quality:** Rock Mass Classification systems (RMR, GSI, Q-system) assess discontinuities and intact rock strength to determine if conventional or mechanized methods are suitable [E004].

* **Groundwater:** The presence, pressure, and flow of groundwater influence method selection. High permeability may favor Slurry Machines, while low permeability or high fines content may favor EPBMs. Groundwater control (dewatering, freezing) is also a factor [E002][E005].

* **Geological Hazards:** The presence of faults, squeezing ground, methane gas, boulders, or liquefiable soils requires specific methods (e.g., avoiding faults where possible, using specialized TBMs for boulders) [E002][E013].
* **Ground Behavior:** Factors such as standup time, plasticity index (sticky clays), and particle size distribution dictate the choice between open-face and closed-face machines [E002][E005].
**2. Geometrical and Project Parameters**

* **Tunnel Length:** TBM methods are generally more competitive for long tunnels (typically >3–5 km) due to high mobilization costs, whereas conventional methods are often more economical for short tunnels [E010].

* **Cross-Section and Diameter:** The size of the excavation affects volume, muck removal, and equipment requirements. Regular cross-sections favor TBMs, while non-uniform sections may favor conventional methods [E010][E020].
* **Depth and Cover:** Shallow tunnels often use cut-and-cover, while deeper tunnels may require mined methods. Sufficient cover is required for TBM operation to manage ground movements [E001][E002].
* **Alignment and Geometry:** The tunnel's alignment, curvature, and required grade can influence the choice of profile and method [E002][E009].
**3. Environmental and Site Constraints**

* **Surface Impact:** Methods are selected to minimize impact on traffic, air quality, noise, and utilities. Bored/mined tunnels are preferred where surface excavation is not feasible or acceptable [E001][E002].

* **Sensitive Facilities:** Proximity to historical landmarks, buildings, or utilities requires methods that minimize vibration and settlement (e.g., mined excavation over cut-and-cover if contamination is present) [E002].
* **Logistics and Site Configuration:** The availability of space for equipment, muck disposal logistics, and site constraints influence the choice [E002][E013].
**4. Economic and Risk Factors**
* **Cost:** The total cost, including capital investment (e.g., TBM purchase vs. lower initial cost of conventional methods), advance rate, and contingencies, drives the selection [E004][E010].

* **Risk Management:** Risk assessments consider construction risks, ground variability, and potential for delays. Thorough geotechnical investigations help reduce uncertainty in method selection [E002][E003].
* **Contractor Experience:** The specific experience and logistics of the contractor can influence the final choice, sometimes requiring a compromise or dual-mode machine [E005].
**5. Specific Method Requirements**
* **Soil Grading:** For soft ground TBMs, the percentage of fines and permeability determine whether an EPBM or Slurry Machine is appropriate [E005].
* **Support Needs:** The required support system (e.g., precast segments vs. cast-in-place concrete) is linked to the excavation method [E008].

Emergency response and evacuation in road tunnels are managed through a combination of immediate operational actions, engineered infrastructure, and coordinated protocols between tunnel operators and emergency services.

**Immediate Response Actions** Upon detection of an incident (fire, collision, or hazardous spill), the tunnel operator must immediately close the tunnel roadway to nonessential vehicles and stop traffic at the entrance [E001][E004]. The operator activates emergency systems, including ventilation to control smoke and provide tenable escape routes, and notifies first responders (fire, police, emergency medical services) via direct lines [E001][E004][E006]. Variable message boards and loudspeakers are used to initialize warnings and provide evacuation instructions to users [E004][E016].

**Evacuation and Self-Rescue** Self-rescue is encouraged as the primary response before emergency services arrive [E001][E004]. Motorists are directed to exit the tunnel in the direction of travel if they are in front of the accident site [E001]. Occupants trapped behind fire and debris must evacuate on foot using designated escape routes [E001]. Effective evacuation relies on intuitive wall signage, audible messages, and lighting that direct users to cross passages, portals, or areas of refuge [E001]. Signs displaying the direction and distance to the nearest emergency exit are considered most effective [E001].
**Engineering Infrastructure for Evacuation** Tunnels are equipped with specific infrastructure to facilitate safe egress:

* **Emergency Exits and Cross-Passages:** Functional, clearly marked escape routes are provided at regular intervals. In twin-tube tunnels, cross-passages to the adjacent tube serve as safe havens and should be located no more than 656 feet (200 m) apart [E003]. These passages require fire-rated construction and self-closing doors [E003].
* **Walkways:** Emergency walkways should be at least 3.6 feet (1.12 m) wide and protected from traffic [E003].
* **Breakdown Bays:** Provided in tunnels longer than 900 meters (or under special conditions from 600 m) to allow vehicles to pull over safely [E005].
* **Ventilation:** Emergency ventilation systems control smoke back-layering and pressurize escape routes to repel smoke and superheated gases [E001][E003].

**Coordination with Emergency Responders** Formal training programs and joint emergency response plans are developed by tunnel operators, safety departments, and responders (fire, police, EMS) [E002]. These plans include protocols for reporting, scene protection, limiting traffic, and activating emergency systems [E002]. An interorganizational memorandum of understanding (MOU) typically defines resource sharing [E002]. Responders coordinate with the tunnel operator to access the scene, often using emergency exits or portals, and manage the incident while ensuring they do not impede evacuating users [E006].

**Post-Incident Procedures** After the incident is resolved and conditions are safe, the tunnel undergoes a thorough inspection for structural damage [E001]. The tunnel is cleared of debris and damaged vehicles, and pavement repairs are made before being restored to service [E001].
Based on the provided evidence, measures to reduce the consequences of a fire in a road tunnel include:
**Detection and Incident Management**
* **Automatic Incident Detection (AID) Systems:** These systems reduce detection and intervention delays, which is critical for enabling self-rescue by road users [E007][E012].
* **Fire Detection Systems:** Automated systems using flame, smoke, or heat sensors provide rapid notification to monitoring stations, triggering emergency responses [E006].
* **Surveillance and SCADA:** Video surveillance, fire/smoke detectors, and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems facilitate rapid detection and response [E005].
**Ventilation and Smoke Control**
* **Emergency Ventilation:** Mechanical ventilation systems (longitudinal or transverse) are used to exhaust smoke, control superheated gases, and provide tenable escape routes [E005].
* **Longitudinal Ventilation:** While not always mandatory if other safety measures are present, longitudinal ventilation (using jet fans or central fans) helps manage smoke spread [E007][E008].
* **Pressurization:** Ventilation can be used to pressurize escape routes to repel smoke and superheated gases [E005].
**Structural and Egress Measures**

* **Emergency Exits:** The presence of multiple emergency exits (e.g., two exits) is important for ensuring an acceptable level of safety, particularly in tunnels without ventilation, by facilitating self-rescue [E007][E012].
* **Cross Passages:** Providing cross passages at reduced intervals (e.g., every 250 m) can lower societal risk by providing safer egress options [E014].
* **Emergency Doors:** Airtight but unlocked emergency doors between parallel tunnels allow trapped personnel to escape smoke-filled tubes [E003].
* **Rescue Chambers:** Fully equipped chambers with independent air supplies and insulation can be deployed along the tunnel during construction to provide refuge [E002].
**Fire Suppression and Protection Systems**
* **Suppression Systems:** Fire protection systems include standpipes, sprinklers, deluge systems (water-based or foam-based), and water mist systems [E005][E006].

* **Equipment Safety:** Requiring fire suppression systems for all underground equipment, conveyor belt motors, and storage magazines; using only retardant materials and hydraulic fluids on underground equipment [E002].
* **Fire Extinguishers:** Providing accessible fire extinguishers and sprinkler systems as part of modern tunnel facility protection [E005].
**Operational and Signage Measures**

* **Intuitive Signage:** Wall signage, audible messages, and lights directing escapees to cross passages, portals, and areas of refuge increase survivability. Signs displaying direction and distance to the nearest emergency exit are most effective [E005].
* **Strobe Lights:** Placing strobe lights around exit doors, especially at lower levels under smoke, to identify exit routes during fires [E008].
* **Emergency Response Plans:** Site-specific plans involving stakeholders (fire, police, management) to assess emergencies, close roadways, adjust ventilation, and notify responders [E015].
* **Drills:** Conducting periodic drills for conditions such as fires, evacuations, and hazardous cargo releases [E005].

* **Traffic Management:** Implementing operational measures for dangerous goods, such as flashing warning lights, escort vehicles, speed limits, and overtaking bans in tunnels of specific lengths [E013].
* **Self-Rescue Encouragement:** Encouraging self-rescue (evacuation on foot) before emergency responders arrive, particularly for those trapped behind the fire [E005].
**Risk Assessment and Design**
* **Scenario Analysis:** Using risk analysis models (e.g., TuRisMo) to evaluate the effectiveness of safety measures, such as reducing vehicle velocity or adding cross passages [E014].

The regulatory requirements for transporting dangerous goods (DG) through road tunnels are primarily governed by the ADR Agreement and EU Directive 2004/54/EC, implemented through national laws such as the Austrian Road Tunnel Safety Law.

**Tunnel Categorization and Restrictions** The ADR Agreement mandates that national competent authorities categorize tunnels into five categories (A–E) based on risk assessments considering three major dangers: explosion, release of toxic gas/volatile liquid, and fire [E001][E005]. The categories impose specific restrictions on DG transport:
* **Category A:** No restrictions for the transport of dangerous goods [E001][E005].
* **Category B:** Restrictions apply to DG which may lead to a very large explosion [E001][E005].
* **Category C:** Restrictions apply to DG leading to a very large explosion, large explosion, or large toxic release; also restricts goods banned in Category B [E001][E005].
* **Category D:** Restrictions apply to DG leading to a very large explosion, large explosion, large toxic release, or large fire; also restricts goods banned in Category C [E001][E005].
* **Category E:** Restrictions apply to all DG except specific UN numbers (2919, 3291, 3331, 3359, and 3373) [E001][E005].

Based on the provided evidence, the legal obligations of a tunnel operator (often referred to as Tunnel Manager, Tunnel Management Office [TMO], or DoR depending on the jurisdiction) include:
**Organizational and Safety Management (EU Directive 2004/54/EC)**
* **Day-to-Day Safety:** The Tunnel Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation and safety of each tunnel [E003].

* **Safety Documentation:** The Tunnel Manager must compile safety documentation that describes all preventive and safeguard measures, adapted to each stage (design, commissioning, operation), serving as a communication tool and the basis for all safety procedures [E001].
* **Appointment of Personnel:** The Tunnel Manager must nominate an Independent Safety Officer who controls and supervises all preventive and safeguard measures [E003].

* **Emergency Procedures:** The Administrative Authority (appointed by Member States) defines the procedure for immediate tunnel closure in an emergency, while the Tunnel Manager secures safety for users during normal operation and emergencies [E001].
**Operational and Maintenance Duties (Nepal MoU / General Standards)**

* **Inspection:** The operator (DoR) is responsible for carrying out daily routine inspections of the tunnel [E012]. This includes monitoring traffic, accidents, and fire incidents continuously (round-the-clock) [E012].

* **Maintenance:** The operator is responsible for the routine maintenance of the tunnel structure and installed facilities, ensuring they are kept in good condition through repair and replacement programs [E012].

* **Immediate Action:** The operator must maintain an immediate action team to respond to vehicle breakdowns, accidents, fire incidents, or facility malfunctions to ensure smooth tunnel functioning [E012].

* **Vehicle Control:** The operator has the authority and obligation to control vehicles carrying dangerous materials, as well as trucks exceeding height or weight limits. They must have the authority to stop vehicles deemed detrimental to tunnel safety [E012].

* **Traffic Police Coordination:** The TMO must coordinate with traffic police regarding violations of traffic rules (e.g., speed limits, overtaking prohibitions). The TMO requests the police to control violating vehicles (arrest/penalty) for matters outside the TMO's delegated powers, while handling monitoring and instruction for delegated matters [E005].

* **Accident Investigation:** The TMO must request the traffic police to investigate accident causes and take legal action, while simultaneously regulating lanes, closing roads, and removing damaged vehicles to prevent secondary accidents [E005].

* **Fire Department Coordination:** The TMO must coordinate with the Fire Department of Local Government Units (LGUs) to determine delegated powers for fire-fighting activities. If the TMO cannot extinguish a fire within its delegated powers, it must request the dispatch of the fire department [E005].

* **Hazardous Material Transport:** The TMO must coordinate with the Land Transportation Department and Police regarding vehicle control (height, weight, hazardous materials) within its delegated powers [E005].

* **Inspection Policies:** The tunnel inspection organization is responsible for developing and maintaining inspection policies, including tunnel-specific inspections, functional system tests, and critical system checks [E002].

PIARC (Dünya Karayolu Birliği) raporlarına ve ilgili çalışmalarına göre, karayolu tünellerinde risk analizi şu temel prensipler ve yöntemlerle yapılır:

**1. Temel Tanım ve Amaç** Risk analizi, tünel güvenliğini iyileştirmek ve optimize etmek için kullanılan önemli bir araçtır. Olasılığı düşük olsa da büyük kaza sonuçlarının (can kaybı, yapı hasarı, ekonomik kayıp) ağır olduğu durumlarda, riskleri belirlemek ve yönetmek için kullanılır [E002][E004]. Analiz, tehlikelerin (hazards) belirlenmesini ve her bir tehlikenin olasılığı ile sonuçlarının tahmin edilmesini içerir. Risk, olasılık ve sonuçların çarpımı olarak belirlenir [E002][E004].
**2. Risk Analiz Süreci Adımları** Risk analizi prosesi genellikle dört ana adımdan oluşur:
* Sistemin tanımlanması (Definition of the system) [E008].
* Tehlike tanımlama (Hazard identification) [E008].
* Olasılık analizi (Probability analysis) [E008].
* Sonuç analizi (Consequence analysis) [E008].
**3. Kullanılan Yaklaşımlar (Metodolojiler)** PIARC, risk değerlendirmesi için iki ana yaklaşım ailesi sunar:

* **Senaryo Tabanlı Yaklaşım (Scenario-based approach):** Belirli bir d ilgili senaryonun frekansı ve/veya sonuçları açısından analiz edildiği yaklaşımdır. Her bir senaryo için risk tahmini ayrı ayrı yapılır [E002][E004]. Bu yöntem, tünelin belirli bir özelliğine veya olayına odaklanır.

* **Sistem Tabanlı Yaklaşım (System-based approach):** Tüneli etkileyen tüm ilgili senaryoları kapsayan entegre bir süreçte genel sistemi incelediği için tünelin tamamına uygulanan risk değerlerini elde etmeyi amaçlar [E002][E004].
**4. Uygulanan Spesifik Yöntemler ve Modeller** PIARC, farklı ülkelerde uygulanan ve bilimsel temelli birçok yöntem olduğunu belirtir. Öne çıkan modeller şunlardır:
* **Avusturya TuRisMo Modeli:** Tünel risk analizi modeli [E004][E005].
* **Hollanda Senaryo Analizi:** Yol tünelleri için deterministik, senaryo tabanlı bir risk analizi yöntemidir [E004][E018].

* **Hollanda TUNPRIM Modeli:** Kaza, yangın, patlama ve toksik sızıntılar için olay ağacı (event tree) analizi kullanan bir EQR (Quantitative Risk Assessment - K nicel risk değerlendirmesi) yöntemidir [E018].

* **Fransız Spesifik Tehlike İncelemesi (Étude Spécifique des Dangers):** Senaryo tabanlı, esnek bir yöntemdir; duman hareketi veya kullanıcı davranışı gibi nicel elementleri entegre edebilir [E001][E018].

* **OECD/PIARC DG-QRA Modeli:** Tehlikeli madde taşımacılığı için geliştirilmiş nicel risk değerlendirmesi modelidir. Toplumsal risk (EV ve FN eğrileri) ve bireysel risk hesaplamaları yapar [E013][E019].
* **İtalyan Yol Tüneli Risk Analizi:** Belirli bir ülkenin uyguladığı yöntemlerden biridir [E004].
**5. Risk Değerlendirme Kriterleri** Risk analizi sonuçları, risk değerlendirmesi (risk evaluation) aşamasında şu kriterlere göre değerlendirilir:
* Uzman yargısı (Expert judgement) [E004][E008].
* Senaryo ile ilgili kriterler (Örn: senaryo olasılık eşikleri veya güvenli yere kaçış süresi) [E004].
* Bireysel risk (Belirli bir kişinin maruz kaldığı yıllık ölüm olasılığı) [E004].
* Toplumsal risk (Tüneldeki yıllık ortalama ölüm sayısı veya sıklık-ölüm sayısı (F-N) eğrisi) [E004][E008].

**6. Yöntem Seçimi ve Esneklik** Hangi metodolojinin uygun olduğu; tünelin özelliklerine, mevcut verilere ve risk analizi yapma spesifik amaçlarına bağlıdır. Hiçbir yöntem pratikte "en iyi" olarak kabul edilmez; durumun gerektirdiği analiz düzeyine, problemin doğasına ve mevcut kaynaklara göre seçim yapılması gerekir [E002][E004]. An Earth Pressure Balance (EPB) Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) is a type of pressurized-face closed shield machine predominantly utilized for large diameter soft ground tunneling [E003].
It is specifically designed to operate in soft ground, particularly where the soil is silty and contains a high percentage of fines [E005].

claim_text: Key functions and applications include:
* **Face Stability:** It uses a closed chamber (bulkhead) to balance groundwater and/or collapsing soil pressure at the tunnel face [E003][E004].

* **Soil Types:** It is suitable for clay, clayey soils, and silty sand soils, especially those located below the water table [E003][E004]. It is considered best for sandy soils with acceptable conditions [E003][E004].

* **Mechanism:** It controls muck removal and maintains face pressure by using a screw discharger with a cone valve (or similar means) to form a "sand plug" [E003][E004]. This plug helps balance the earth pressure and control groundwater inflows [E005].
* **Groundwater Control:** The design assists in controlling groundwater inflows, which is critical when the ground has a high percentage of fines [E005].
In contrast to Slurry Face Machines (SFM), which transmit pressure hydraulically, an EPB machine transmits pressure to the face mechanically through soil grains [E004].

In Turkish tunnel contracts, shotcrete work is measured and paid for based on the following principles:

**1. Measurement Method (Volume Calculation)** The quantity is calculated in cubic meters ($m^3$) based on the volume of shotcrete applied beyond a specified baseline thickness. The measurement is derived by multiplying the cross-sectional area (calculated from the "Theoretical Excavation Line" perimeter and the excess thickness) by the tunnel length for the relevant soil class [E001][E002].
The baseline thicknesses added to the project-specified shotcrete layer to account for unavoidable excavation voids are:
* **5 cm** for soil classes A1, A2, and B1 [E001][E007].
* **7.5 cm** for soil classes B2 and B3 [E001][E007].
* **10 cm** for soil classes C1, C2, and C3 [E001][E007].
**2. Payment Terms**
* **Inside the Tunnel:** Payment is made based on the unit price for "Tunnel Shotcrete (Shotcrete) Construction (with Concrete Plant)" per cubic meter ($m^3$) [E001][E002].

* **Outside the Tunnel (Portals):** Payment is made based on the unit price for "Shotcrete Construction" per ton, determined by weighing the shotcrete mixture at the concrete plant before water is added [E002][E007].
**3. Specific Payment Rules and Exclusions**

* **Local Voids (< 2 $m^3$):** Local excavation voids smaller than 2 cubic meters are filled with concrete (minimum class C16/20) but receive no separate payment, as they are considered within construction and deformation tolerances [E001][E007].

* **Large Voids (≥ 2 $m^3$):** Unavoidable voids of 2 cubic meters or larger, resulting from unfavorable geological conditions (not the contractor's fault), are filled with concrete (minimum class C16/20) upon administration instruction. However, payment is made from the "C16/20 Concrete" position unit price, not the shotcrete price [E001].

* **Temporary Support:** Shotcrete applied for temporary support (e.g., at the tunnel face) that is later removed and discarded is included in the excavation unit price and receives no separate payment [E001][E002].
* **Thin Shotcrete:** Fine shotcrete included in the unit price is not calculated separately [E001].
* **Excess Thickness:** No payment is made for shotcrete thickness applied beyond the baseline amounts specified for each soil class to fill unavoidable voids [E001][E007].
* **No Additional Payments:** No additional payments are made for "inflation" or other names regarding excavation, production, transport, materials, or labor [E001][E007].

* **Very Large IEDs:** Delivered by ship, barge, or boat (e.g., depth charges dropped above an immersed tube tunnel) [E003].

Additionally, threats are classified as **Vehicle-borne improvised explosive devices (VBIED)** including land-borne vehicles (truck bombs) and waterborne vehicles (boat bombs), and **Hand-emplaced IEDs (HEIED)** such as contact explosive devices like satchel demolition charges or shaped charges [E005].
Based on the evidence provided, the Traffic Control Center follows these procedures after receiving a report or confirming via CCTV that a traffic accident (or vehicle breakdown) has occurred:
* **Communication and Confirmation:** The center communicates with the Patrol Team to confirm the details of the incident on-site [E001].
* **Traffic Regulation:** It conducts lane regulation and other measures to prevent further incidents [E001].
* **Information Display:** It displays information about the incident on emergency information boards [E001].
* **Vehicle Removal:** If necessary, it requests the Action Team to remove the accident vehicles [E001].
* **Emergency Dispatch:** It instructs the dispatch of an ambulance [E001].
* **Agency Coordination:** It communicates with related agencies, including traffic police and hospitals [E001].
* **Restoration:** It instructs the Maintenance Section to conduct emergency repairs to restore traffic [E001].

Additionally, other evidence notes that the head of the monitoring team must immediately decide whether to inform the Action Team, Fire Department, and/or Police based on the severity of the major incidents [E003].
Patlatmalı kazı (delme ve patlatma) sonrasında uygulanan işlemler ve sıralaması, kaynaklarda şu şekilde belirtilmiştir:
1. **Havalandırma:** Patlama dumanlarının temizlenmesi için havalandırma yapılır [E016].
2. **Güvenlik Kontrolü ve Ölçüm:** Patlama sonrası oluşan titreşim değerleri vibrometre ile ölçülür ve kaydedilir [E002][E004].
3. **Kazı (Hafriyat):** Patlayarak kırılan kaya (hafriyat) temizlenir ve taşınır [E013][E016].
4. **Ölçüm ve Raporlama:** Tünel ilerledikçe yüzey ölçümü, jeolojik haritalama ve loglama yapılır; süreksizlikler ve su durumu kayıt altına alınır [E001][E013].
5. **Ölçekleme (Scaling):** Taşınması gereken gevşemiş kaya parçaları, tavan ve duvarlardan temizlenir [E016].
6. **Birincil Destekleme:**
* Sürenler (rock bolts) çakılır veya enjeksiyon boruları yerleştirilir [E014][E018].
* Püskürtme beton (shotcrete) uygulanır [E014][E016].
* Çelik iksa (steel sets) ve/veya hasır çelik döşenir [E014].
* Gerekli görülen durumlarda ikinci kat destekleme elemanları yerleştirilir [E005].
7. **İkincil Destekleme (Kapaklama):** Birincil desteklemenin ardından, proje gereği ikinci kaplama (genellikle betonarme) yapılır [E013][E016].
Kazı döngüsü (tunneling cycle) genel olarak şu adımları izler: Delme -> Patlayıcı doldurma -> Patlatma -> Havalandırma -> Hafriyat -> Ölçekleme -> Birincil destek -> Ölçüm/Kontrol [E016].
Patlayıcı madde kullanımında geçerli güvenlik kuralları, taşıma, depolama, ateşleme prosedürleri ve çevresel koruma başlıkları altında aşağıda özetlenmiştir:
**1. Taşıma Kuralları**
* Patlayıcı maddelerin işletme sahası dışından taşınması için 87/12028 sayılı tüzüğün 53. maddesine göre Taşıma İzin Belgesi alınmalıdır [E001].
* İşletme sınırları içinde, taşıtla taşınan ve 250 kg'ı geçmeyen aynı işyeri sınırları içerisindeki taşımalarda işyeri amirinin sorumluluğunda izin belgesi almaya gerek yoktur [E001].

* Patlayıcı maddelerle kapsüllerin aynı taşıma aracı üzerinde taşınması yasaktır; ancak 50 km'yi geçmeyen ve toplam ağırlığı 300 kg'ı geçmeyen taşımalar için, kapsüller ile patlayıcı maddelerin farklı bölümlerde olması koşuluyla aynı araçta taşıma yapılabilir [E001].
* Taşıma, sorumlu bir memurun ve güvenlik güçlerinin nezareti altında yapılacaktır [E001].
**2. Depolama Kuralları**
* Patlayıcı maddeler sadece yasal izinleri alınmış ve Patlayıcı Madde Satın Alma ve Kullanma İzin Belgesi'nde belirtilen depolarda korunmalıdır [E001].
* Depolar sürekli, geçici ve gezici olmak üzere 3 gruba ayrılır; yapımı, güvenlik mesafesi, kapasite ve havalandırma gibi konularda ilgili tüzük hükümlerine uyulmalıdır [E001].
* Yüklenici, patlayıcı maddeleri ruhsatlı ve kapsül için özel bir bölümü bulunan bir depo veya ambar içinde muhafaza etmelidir [E011].
* Nitrogliserin ve amonyum nitrat bazlı patlayıcılar 32°C'nin üzerinde depolandıklarında bozulma gösterir; ANFO ise neme karşı duyarlıdır ve bu ortamlarda bekletilmemelidir [E017].
**3. Kullanım ve Ateşleme Prosedürleri**
* Yetkili olmayan hiç kimse patlayıcı madde kullanamaz; ateşleyicilerin geçerli 'Ateşleyici Yeterlik Belgesi'ne (yer altı/tünel için C-sınıfı) sahip olması gerekir [E001].
* Lağım delikleri ancak ateşlenecekleri zaman doldurulmalı, kartuşlar biçimleri bozulmadan kullanılmalı ve deliklere zorla sokulmamalıdır [E001].
* Elektrikle ateşlemede bağlantılar önce gözle, sonra uygun patlatma ohmmetresi ile kontrol edilmelidir; test sırasında kesinlikle manyeto kullanılmamalıdır [E001].
* Ölçülen devre direnci, manyeto kapasitesinin yarısı kadar olmalıdır [E001].
* Ateşleme işi sadece manyeto ile yapılmalı; pil, akü veya şehir gerilimi gibi kaynaklar kullanılmamalıdır [E001].
* Patlatma öncesi emniyet sahası belirlenmeli, kırmızı bayraklarla işaret verilmeli ve son işareti almadan emniyet sahasına kimse girmemelidir [E001].
* Elektrik yüklü şimşekli havalarda veya yıldırım düşme tehlikesi olan durumlarda patlatma operasyonu kesinlikle durdurulmalıdır [E001].
* Fırtınalı havalarda patlayıcıların kullanımı, yerleştirilmesi ve ateşlenmesi yapılmamalıdır [E011].
**4. Patlamayan Delikler ve Atılma Sonrası İşlemler**
* Ateşlemeden sonra patlamayan lağım bulunursa; fitille ateşlemede en az 1 saat, elektrikle ateşlemede 5 dakika geçmeden alan kimse girmemelidir [E001].
* Patlamamış patlayıcı madde artıkları, nezaretçi sorumluluğunda ve patlamamış deliğin en az 30 cm yakınında paralel yeni bir delik açılarak patlatılmalıdır [E001].
* Pasaların elle kaldırılması sırasında kürek, kazma gibi metal ve sivri uçlu aletler kullanılmamalıdır [E001].
**5. Çevresel Koruma ve Denetim**
* Patlatma işlemi, güvenlik güçlerinden izin alınarak, yöre halkına duyuru yapılarak ve ÇED/PTD raporunda belirtilen patlayıcı miktarı aşılmadan yapılmalıdır [E006].
* Patlatma dizaynı, mühendise sunulan detaylı planlar (delme paterni, patlayıcı tipi, gecikmeler vb.) doğrultusunda onaylanmalıdır [E011].
* Titreşim ölçümleri vibrometre ile yapılmalı; amplitüt değeri 0,20 mm ve pik tanecik hızı 25 mm/s'yi geçmemelidir [E011].
* Oturma mahallerinin 100 m civarında mühendis özel onayı olmadan patlamaya izin verilmez [E011].
* Beton dökümünün bitişinden itibaren 4-24 saat boyunca patlamadan kaynaklanan titreşimlere maruz bırakılmamalıdır [E011].
* Kontrolü patlatmalarda düşük gaz ürünlü patlayıcılar kullanılmalı ve ağız sıkılamasından kaçınılmalıdır [E004].
Şartnameye göre püskürtme beton uygulaması aşağıdaki esaslara tabidir:
**1. Ön Hazırlık ve Yüzey Temizliği**

* Püskürtme işlemi öncesinde kaya yüzeyi, basınçlı hava ve nozuldan verilen su ile temizlenmelidir. Temizleme işlemi tünelin üst (tepe) kısmından başlayarak sistematik olarak her iki yandan aşağıya doğru yapılmalıdır [E014][E016].
* Zayıf ve gevşek kaya parçaları yüzeyden uzaklaştırılmalı, serbest parçacık ve toz kalmamalıdır [E001].
* Yüzey nemli tutulmalı ancak betonun su/çimento oranını etkileyecek serbest su bulunmamalıdır; aksi halde drenaj sağlanmalıdır [E001].
* Su yalıtımı uygulanacaksa, membran tesbiti için minimum 5 cm'lik püskürtme beton kaplaması yapılmalı ve çıkıntılar (çelik çubuk, bulon vb.) kapatılmalıdır [E009].
**2. Uygulama Tekniği ve Nozul Ayarları**
* Püskürtme işlemine aşağıdan başlanıp yukarı doğru devam edilmelidir [E005][E006].
* Nozul doğrultusu püskürtme yüzeyine daima dik olmalıdır; eğik tutulması malzeme kaybını (GSK/rebound) artırır [E005][E006].
* Optimum zemin-nozul mesafesi korunmalıdır: Tamir işlerinde 0,5-1,0 m; kaya destekte robotla idare ediliyorsa 1,0-2,0 m; elle tutuluyorsa 0,5-1,5 m tavsiye edilir [E005][E006].
* Beton nozuldan kesintisiz ve sabit akışla çıkmalıdır; akış kesintiye uğrarsa püskürtme durdurulmalıdır [E005][E006].
* İşlem aşağıdan yukarıya doğru, ince katmanlar halinde (ilk tabaka 60-100 mm) uygulanmalı, her katman priz almadan sonrakine geçilmemelidir [E014][E016].
**3. Malzeme ve Karışım Özellikleri**
* Maksimum su/çimento oranı 0,50'yi aşmayacaktır [E001].
* Minimum çimento dozajı 350 kg/m³ olarak uygulanacaktır [E001].
* Yaş sistemde önerilen çökme (slump) değeri 100-200 mm arasındadır [E007][E014].
* Priz hızlandırıcı katkı kullanılıyorsa dozaj, üretici limitleri içinde tutularak en düşük seviyeye indirilmelidir; yüksek doz reboundu artırır [E014][E016].
**4. Katman Kalınlığı ve Donatı Gömülmesi**
* Bir defada uygulanacak maksimum püskürtme beton kalınlığı 15 cm'yi geçmeyecektir [E014][E016].
* Çelik iksa, hasır çelik ve diğer donatılar püskürtme beton içerisine gömülmeli; minimum beton pas payı 20 mm olmalıdır [E014][E016].
* Sekme (GSK) malzemesi yapımda tekrar kullanılmayacak ve çalışma alanından temizlenecektir [E014][E016].
**5. Kür ve Koruma**
* Priz hızlandırıcı kullanılıyorsa kürleme işlemi 20 dakika içinde, kullanılmıyorsa 1 saat içinde başlatılmalıdır [E003][E004].
* Islak kürleme (su ile) en az 7 gün boyunca devam etmelidir [E003][E004].
* Püskürtme betonun basınç dayanımı en az 5 MPa'a ulaşana kadar tabii dona karşı korunmalıdır [E003][E004].
